text: The witness testifies in the hill dialect; Mira is the court's only interpreter of it, so her rendering enters the record as verbatim and cannot be checked against the source.
The legal case against Radan is thin: the one witness who could place him at the sluice is dead. A faithful rendering in the innocent sense acquits him.
Years ago Radan showed the raiders the sluice path to the upper village; the flood and the raid that followed killed its people. It is true, and it cannot be proven in law.
In the hill dialect the verb for what happened at the sluice carries two senses — 'he was led to it' and 'he led them to it' — parted only by breath and by the choice of whoever carries it across.
Josif is choosing dialect words whose faithful rendering damns Radan, using Mira as the instrument he will not be seen to be.
